title: Obadiah
subtitle: The Vision of Obadiah - Key Notes, Cross-References, and Messianic Connections (WEB)

items.value: Obadiah is the shortest book in the Hebrew Scriptures: twenty-one verses, one vision, about one nation. It is the last chapter of a rivalry that began in a mother's womb, between Jacob and Esau.
It is short enough to read in two minutes, and it says more about pride than many long books.

sections.heading: How this study is put together

items.value: Each of the shortest books in the Bible is one chapter long, so each one is a complete study in a single guide, laid out the same way as every other book in this series.

values: **Key Notes** - observations worth having in hand before you read, each ending with the verses it comes from.
**Key Cross-References** - passages that stand behind or alongside the text, grouped by theme.
**Messianic Connections** - places where the text reaches back into the Hebrew Scriptures or points ahead to the Messiah. Where an entry is a pattern rather than a prediction, the note says so.
**For Further Study** - places to go deeper.
**Introduction** - the book read as a whole before you read it in parts.
**The text itself**, printed in full in the World English Bible, with footnote markers on the verses the references belong to.

items.value: Every scripture reference is a live link to the World English Bible on BibleGateway. In the app, tapping a footnote marker shows the full text of the passages cited and a line on why they connect.

sections.heading: A note on the divine names

items.value: In the notes and introductions this study uses **Yahweh** for the covenant name of God and **Yahshua** for the Messiah. The printed scripture text is never altered; the World English Bible stands exactly as the translators set it, so our own speech and the translator's work stay visibly distinct.
Nothing is known of Obadiah except his name, which means servant of Yahweh. The book gives no king's reign and no father's name.

The day it describes - strangers carrying Jerusalem away, Edom standing by and then joining in - fits the fall of Jerusalem to Babylon, and Psalm 137 remembers Edom's part in that day. Some place the book earlier, at a lesser attack on Jerusalem. Its first nine verses run closely parallel to Jeremiah 49, sometimes word for word.

Edom was Esau's people, settled in the red rock country south of the Dead Sea, with cities cut into the cliffs. The Torah told Israel not to abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother; Edom refused Israel passage on the way out of Egypt, and the bitterness never healed.
Edom disappeared as a nation. Its people, the Idumeans, were later absorbed into Judea, and King Herod the Great was one of them.

values: **Verses 1-9** - the pride of Edom, and Yahweh bringing it down.
**Verses 10-14** - the charge: violence done to a brother on the day of his disaster.
**Verses 15-16** - the day of Yahweh on all the nations: as you have done, it will be done to you.
**Verses 17-21** - deliverance on Mount Zion, the house of Jacob and the house of Joseph together, and the kingdom that will be Yahweh's.

chapters.heading: OBADIAH - The Pride of Edom, a Brother Who Watched, and the Kingdom Will Be Yahweh's
chapters.title: The Pride of Edom, a Brother Who Watched, and the Kingdom Will Be Yahweh's
keyNotes: Obadiah means servant of Yahweh. Nothing else is known about him - no father, no town, no king's reign. The vision is the whole of what we have (Obadiah 1:1).

Edom is Esau. The twins fought in Rebekah's womb, and Yahweh told her two nations were in it and the elder would serve the younger. Obadiah is the last chapter of that rivalry (Obadiah 1:6, 1:10, Genesis 25:23).

Verses 1 to 9 run closely parallel to Jeremiah 49:7-16, sometimes word for word. Either one prophet drew on the other, or both drew on a word already known. Two witnesses saying the same thing (Obadiah 1:1-9, Jeremiah 49:16).
"An ambassador is sent among the nations." Yahweh is gathering the nations against Edom. The attack comes from His word before it comes from any army (Obadiah 1:1).
"I have made you small among the nations." Edom thought itself great. Yahweh calls it small, and speaks as if it were already done (Obadiah 1:2).
"The pride of your heart has deceived you." Pride is not only a sin. It is a liar. It told Edom it was safe (Obadiah 1:3, Proverbs 16:18).

Edom's cities were cut into the red sandstone cliffs south of the Dead Sea, reached through narrow gorges. Petra, carved into the rock, later stood in that same country. Who will bring me down? was a reasonable question about the walls. It was a fatal one about the heart (Obadiah 1:3).

"Though your nest is set among the stars." It echoes the king of Babylon in Isaiah 14: I will exalt my throne above the stars of God. The same pride, and the same answer: brought down (Obadiah 1:4, Isaiah 14:13-15).
Thieves take only what they want, and grape pickers leave gleanings. What is coming to Edom will leave nothing (Obadiah 1:5, Jeremiah 49:9).
"The men of your alliance have... deceived you." Edom trusted its allies. They turned on it. The one who betrays a brother is betrayed by friends (Obadiah 1:7).
"Friends who eat your bread lay a snare under you." The psalm says it of a trusted friend who ate bread with me and lifted up his heel (Obadiah 1:7, Psalm 41:9).
Teman was a region of Edom famous for its wise men. Eliphaz, one of Job's counselors, was a Temanite. Yahweh will destroy the wise men out of Edom (Obadiah 1:8-9, Job 2:11).

"For the violence done to your brother Jacob." The word brother is the charge. The Torah had told Israel: you shall not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother. Edom did not return the kindness (Obadiah 1:10, Deuteronomy 23:7).
Edom had refused Israel passage through its land on the way out of Egypt and came out with the sword, so Israel went around. The grudge was old (Obadiah 1:10, Numbers 20:18-21).
"In the day that you stood on the other side." Standing aloof is the first charge. Watching is where it started (Obadiah 1:11).

The day in view is most likely the fall of Jerusalem to Babylon. The psalmist by the rivers of Babylon remembered the children of Edom crying: raze it, raze it, even to its foundation (Obadiah 1:11, Psalm 137:7).
"Even you were like one of them." A brother who stands by while strangers attack becomes one of the strangers (Obadiah 1:11).

Eight times Yahweh says don't - don't look down, don't rejoice, don't speak proudly, don't enter the gate, don't look on their affliction, don't seize their wealth, don't stand at the crossroads, don't deliver them up. It runs from watching to gloating to looting to handing over (Obadiah 1:12-14).
"Don't rejoice over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction." Proverbs: do not rejoice when your enemy falls, lest Yahweh see it and it displease Him (Obadiah 1:12, Proverbs 24:17-18).
"Don't speak proudly" is literally don't make your mouth great. Pride again, in the mouth (Obadiah 1:12).
"The day of Yahweh is near all the nations!" Edom is the example, not the exception. What is said to Edom is said to everyone who does what Edom did (Obadiah 1:15).

"As you have done, it will be done to you. Your deeds will return upon your own head." It is the Torah's measure for measure, and Paul's whatever a man sows, that he will also reap (Obadiah 1:15, Leviticus 24:19, Galatians 6:7).
"As you have drunk on my holy mountain" - Edom celebrated on Mount Zion after it fell. Now the nations will drink the cup of Yahweh's wrath (Obadiah 1:16, Jeremiah 25:15).
"In Mount Zion, there will be those who escape, and it will be holy." Joel says the same: in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be those who escape (Obadiah 1:17, Joel 2:32).
"The house of Jacob will possess their possessions." What was taken is given back (Obadiah 1:17).

"The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame." Two houses named side by side, Judah under the name of Jacob and the northern tribes under the name of Joseph, burning together. Ezekiel's two sticks, Judah and Joseph, become one in Yahweh's hand (Obadiah 1:18, Ezekiel 37:16).
"Indeed, Yahweh has spoken." The fire is not Jacob's idea. It is Yahweh's word (Obadiah 1:18).

The returning people spread out in every direction: the South takes Esau's mountain, the lowland takes Philistia, Ephraim and Samaria are possessed, Benjamin takes Gilead. The land is given back whole (Obadiah 1:19-20).
Sepharad is an unknown place, perhaps Sardis in Asia Minor. Later Jews used the name for Spain, which is where the word Sephardic comes from (Obadiah 1:20).

"Saviors will go up on Mount Zion." The word is the one used for the judges Yahweh raised up to save Israel: you gave them saviors who saved them out of the hands of their adversaries (Obadiah 1:21, Nehemiah 9:27).

"The kingdom will be Yahweh's." The whole book has been about a nation that thought it could not be brought down. It ends with the only kingdom that will not be. Revelation hears the same announcement: the kingdom of the world has become the Kingdom of our Lord and of His Messiah (Obadiah 1:21, Psalm 22:28, Revelation 11:15).

Edom as a nation disappeared. Its people, the Idumeans, were later absorbed into Judea, and King Herod the Great, who tried to kill the infant Yahshua, was an Idumean. Esau against Jacob one last time (Obadiah 1:18, Matthew 2:16).

intro: Obadiah, the shortest book in the Hebrew Scriptures, is about two brothers. Jacob and Esau fought in Rebekah's womb, and Yahweh told her that two nations were within her and that the elder would serve the younger. Esau became Edom, a people settled in the red rock country south of the Dead Sea, with cities cut into cliffs and reached through narrow gorges, confident that no army could reach them. Who will bring me down to the ground? Edom asks, and Yahweh answers that the pride of its heart has deceived it, and that though it set its nest among the stars He will bring it down. Pride is not only a sin; it is a liar that promises safety.

The charge is the violence done to a brother. The Torah had told Israel not to abhor an Edomite, for he is a brother, and when Jerusalem fell Edom did not act as one. Obadiah traces the descent in a series of prohibitions: standing aloof while strangers carried Jerusalem away, then looking down on Judah's disaster, rejoicing, boasting, entering the gate, seizing the wealth, and standing at the crossroads to cut off and hand over the survivors - from watching to gloating to looting to betrayal. The psalmist by the rivers of Babylon remembered Edom crying raze it to its foundation. The sentence is measure for measure: as you have done, it will be done to you.

Then the book turns. On Mount Zion there will be deliverance, and it will be holy. The house of Jacob will be a fire and the house of Joseph a flame - the two houses named side by side and burning together, as Ezekiel saw the sticks of Judah and Joseph joined in Yahweh's hand - and the returning exiles will possess the land in every direction. The last line belongs to the only kingdom that cannot be brought down: saviors will go up on Mount Zion, and the kingdom will be Yahweh's. History added an epilogue. Edom vanished as a nation; its descendants, the Idumeans, were absorbed into Judea; and an Idumean king, Herod, tried to kill the child born in Bethlehem.

verses.1: The vision of Obadiah. This is what the Lord Yahweh says about Edom. We have heard news from Yahweh, and an ambassador is sent among the nations, saying, “Arise, and let’s rise up against her in battle.
verses.2: Behold, I have made you small among the nations. You are greatly despised.
verses.3: The pride of your heart has deceived you, you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high, who says in his heart, ‘Who will bring me down to the ground?’
verses.4: Though you mount on high as the eagle, and though your nest is set among the stars, I will bring you down from there,” says Yahweh.
verses.5: “If thieves came to you, if robbers by night—oh, what disaster awaits you—wouldn’t they only steal until they had enough? If grape pickers came to you, wouldn’t they leave some gleaning grapes?
verses.6: How Esau will be ransacked! How his hidden treasures are sought out!
verses.7: All the men of your alliance have brought you on your way, even to the border. The men who were at peace with you have deceived you, and prevailed against you. Friends who eat your bread lay a snare under you. There is no understanding in him.”
verses.8: “Won’t I in that day”, says Yahweh, “destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mountain of Esau?
verses.9: Your mighty men, Teman, will be dismayed, to the end that everyone may be cut off from the mountain of Esau by slaughter.
verses.10: For the violence done to your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be cut off forever.
verses.11: In the day that you stood on the other side, in the day that strangers carried away his substance, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots for Jerusalem, even you were like one of them.
verses.12: But don’t look down on your brother in the day of his disaster, and don’t rejoice over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction. Don’t speak proudly in the day of distress.
verses.13: Don’t enter into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity. Don’t look down on their affliction in the day of their calamity, neither seize their wealth on the day of their calamity.
verses.14: Don’t stand in the crossroads to cut off those of his who escape. Don’t deliver up those of his who remain in the day of distress.
verses.15: For the day of Yahweh is near all the nations! As you have done, it will be done to you. Your deeds will return upon your own head.
verses.16: For as you have drunk on my holy mountain, so will all the nations drink continually. Yes, they will drink, swallow down, and will be as though they had not been.
verses.17: But in Mount Zion, there will be those who escape, and it will be holy. The house of Jacob will possess their possessions.
verses.18: The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble. They will burn among them, and devour them. There will not be any remaining to the house of Esau.” Indeed, Yahweh has spoken.
verses.19: Those of the South will possess the mountain of Esau, and those of the lowland, the Philistines. They will possess the field of Ephraim, and the field of Samaria. Benjamin will possess Gilead.
verses.20: The captives of this army of the children of Israel, who are among the Canaanites, will possess even to Zarephath; and the captives of Jerusalem, who are in Sepharad, will possess the cities of the Negev.
verses.21: Saviors will go up on Mount Zion to judge the mountains of Esau, and the kingdom will be Yahweh’s.

cites.text: As for your terror, the pride of your heart has deceived you, O you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, who hold the height of the hill, though you should make your nest as high as the eagle, I will bring you down from there,” says Yahweh.
Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.

3.why: the pride of your heart has deceived you, you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, and pride goes before destruction

cites.text: You said in your heart, “I will ascend into heaven! I will exalt my throne above the stars of God! I will sit on the mountain of assembly, in the far north! I will ascend above the heights of the clouds! I will make myself like the Most High!” Yet you shall be brought down to Sheol, to the depths of the pit.

4.why: I will exalt my throne above the stars of God, yet you shall be brought down

cites.text: If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleaning grapes? If thieves came by night, wouldn’t they steal until they had enough?

5.why: grape gatherers leaving gleanings, and thieves taking only what they want

cites.text: Yahweh said to her, “Two nations are in your womb. Two peoples will be separated from your body. The one people will be stronger than the other people. The elder will serve the younger.”
You shall not abhor an Edomite; for he is your brother. You shall not abhor an Egyptian, because you lived as a foreigner in his land.

10.why: two nations in your womb, the elder serving the younger, and you shall not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother

cites.text: Remember, Yahweh, against the children of Edom, the day of Jerusalem; who said, “Raze it! Raze it even to its foundation!”

Edom said to him, “You shall not pass through me, lest I come out with the sword against you.” The children of Israel said to him, “We will go up by the highway; and if we drink your water, I and my livestock, then I will give its price. Only let me, without doing anything else, pass through on my feet.” He said, “You shall not pass through.” Edom came out against him with many people, and with a strong hand. Thus Edom refused to give Israel passage through his border, so Israel turned away from him.

11.why: remember against the children of Edom the day of Jerusalem, and Edom refusing Israel passage with the sword

cites.text: Don’t rejoice when your enemy falls. Don’t let your heart be glad when he is overthrown; lest Yahweh see it, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him.

As you rejoiced over the inheritance of the house of Israel because it was desolate, so will I do to you. You will be desolate, Mount Seir, and all Edom, even all of it. Then they will know that I am Yahweh.’”

12.why: do not rejoice when your enemy falls, and as you rejoiced over Israel's desolation, so will I do to you

cites.text: If anyone injures his neighbor; as he has done, so shall it be done to him:
Don’t be deceived. God is not mocked, for whatever a man sows, that he will also reap.

15.why: as he has done, so shall it be done to him, and whatever a man sows, that he will also reap

cites.text: For Yahweh, the God of Israel, says to me: “Take this cup of the wine of wrath from my hand, and cause all the nations to whom I send you to drink it.

Thus says your Lord Yahweh, your God who pleads the cause of his people, “Behold, I have taken out of your hand the cup of staggering, even the bowl of the cup of my wrath. You will not drink it any more:

16.why: the cup of the wine of wrath given to the nations, and the cup of staggering taken out of Zion's hand

cites.text: It will happen that whoever will call on Yahweh’s name shall be saved; for in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be those who escape, as Yahweh has said, and among the remnant, those whom Yahweh calls.
It will happen, that he who is left in Zion, and he who remains in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, even everyone who is written among the living in Jerusalem;

17.why: in Mount Zion there will be those who escape, and he who is left in Zion shall be called holy

cites.text: “You, son of man, take one stick, and write on it, ‘For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions.’ Then take another stick, and write on it, ‘For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions.’

“I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph, and I will bring them back; for I have mercy on them; and they will be as though I had not cast them off: for I am Yahweh their God, and I will hear them.

18.why: one stick for Judah and one for Joseph, and I will strengthen the house of Judah and save the house of Joseph

cites.text: In that day I will raise up the tent of David who is fallen, and close up its breaches, and I will raise up its ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old; that they may possess the remnant of Edom, and all the nations who are called by my name,” says Yahweh who does this.

They will fly down on the shoulders of the Philistines on the west. Together they will plunder the children of the east. They will extend their power over Edom and Moab, and the children of Ammon will obey them.

19.why: the fallen tent of David raised up to possess the remnant of Edom, and power extended over Edom and Moab

cites.text: Therefore you delivered them into the hand of their adversaries, who distressed them. In the time of their trouble, when they cried to you, you heard from heaven; and according to your manifold mercies you gave them saviors who saved them out of the hands of their adversaries.
For the kingdom is Yahweh’s. He is the ruler over the nations.
Yahweh will be King over all the earth. In that day Yahweh will be one, and his name one.

21.why: saviors given who saved them from their adversaries, the kingdom is Yahweh's, and Yahweh King over all the earth
